key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant, because both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic efficiency losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect robustness can simplify material optimization.
method: First-principles calculations on a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium.
Quantified Shockley-Read-Hall recombination through both nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture.
Compared recombination trends across defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong suppression of nonradiative recombination due to large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per event, and finds that realistic point-defect concentrations cannot account for device losses.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on computed defect physics, so device-level losses may still involve extrinsic factors beyond the modeled point defects.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
